title: Odile and the Hollow
premise: Casper Iversen, a royal food-taster whose body has become a ledger of poisons, secretly keeps accounts for the Hollow Guild — a syndicate trading in impossible things: bottled memories, borrowed years, the last words of the drowned. When the old gods resume answering prayers, every debt in Casper's ledgers comes due at once, and the usurper King Vael marches on the free cities to claim divinity for himself. Guided by Odile, a disgraced priestess who once brokered the broken covenant between gods and mortals, Casper must reforge that covenant using his own poisoned blood as ink. In the end, Casper pays the final entry in his ledger with his life's remaining years, sealing the gods behind a fairer bargain while Odile leads the free cities to victory over Vael.
about_author: Tamsin Thornbury is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant guild records from coastal free cities, an obsession that seeps into her fiction's obsession with debts and ledgers. She writes fantasy about ordinary functionaries caught in mythic machinery from a drafty house overlooking a grey northern sea.

chapters.title: The Taster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper Iversen's POV. Casper survives another poisoned banquet for the usurper's court while privately balancing the Hollow Guild's impossible accounts, including a debt owed by Odile, a disgraced priestess who buys back her own name. When prayers to the old gods are suddenly answered mid-ritual, one of Casper's recorded transactions manifests physically in the guild vault. Emotional beat: wary competence cracking into dread as the ledgers begin writing back.

chapters.title: What the Gods Owed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Casper and Odile. Fleeing the capital ahead of Vael's inquisitors, they trace the answered prayers to a ruptured covenant: the gods were bound by a bargain Odile herself helped broker and betray. Each unpaid divine debt now fuels Vael's armies with stolen miracles. Casper realizes his poisoned blood is the only solvent that can read the covenant's original terms. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership forged through mutual guilt and grudging respect.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Miracle
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing on Casper. At the besieged free city of Marrowgate, Vael offers the citizens a godhood of his own manufacture, and half the council wants to accept. Odile publicly confesses her betrayal of the covenant to shatter his legitimacy, while Casper infiltrates Vael's warcamp disguised as a tribute-taster, discovering the king has been consuming raw divinity and is rotting from within. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered without guarantee, loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: A Fairer Bargain
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the flooded crypt beneath Marrowgate, Casper rewrites the covenant in his own poisoned blood, offering his accumulated immunities and remaining years as collateral so the gods can answer only freely given prayers. The gods accept; Vael, denied his stolen miracles, crumbles before the allied armies. Odile survives to lead the free cities, carrying Casper's final ledger entry: paid in full. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into covenant — survival's price honored, not erased.
